1: The bevel bands along the G top are chopped into mismatched yellow, white and red segments and the red bar sags and overlaps the white fill, where the art has one continuous gradient bevel. | 2: The G top bevel band changes colour in patches (yellow, white, red) and its stitch direction flips, unlike the smooth gold-to-cream gradient of the art.

1: The L of GOLF is broken into patches of orange, yellow and red with its foot ragged and overlapping the F. | 2: The L of GOLF has fragmented red and orange blocks with a tuft of random stitches at its foot and a patchy stem.

one_reader.note: The O of GOLF is a pile of crossing red, yellow, orange and grey fills with its counter half filled with grey stitches, so the letter does not read as an O.
The TM mark to the right of the F is absent from the render.
The black outline of the swoosh arc has a stepped, saw-toothed edge along both sides where the art is smooth, and it repeats around the whole design.
The lower tip of the swoosh arc ends in a blunt notched point with a kink instead of the art's fine tapering tail.
The right end of the swoosh arc frays into loose white strips and a ragged black edge instead of a clean tapered tip.
The inner counter of the G has its black shadow edge uneven and the red bevel misaligned with the art around the notch.
The T crossbar bevel strips (white, red, yellow) are separate short blocks that do not meet cleanly at the crossbar-stem corner.
The tee yellow flare's stitches fan irregularly and the tip near the right end is a ragged separate fragment.
The long tee stem edges are stair-stepped on both the yellow and black sides.
Long needle-up runs (magenta) cross the whole design between colour blocks, including from the tee bottom up to GOLF and across to the T, which risks visible trims and jump threads.
The O of GOLF is a swirl of mixed-direction fragments with its counter filled by white stitching and red ring, no longer a clean open O with a bevel.
The TM mark to the right of GOLF is absent from the render.
The black outline and shadow along the swoosh are saw-toothed and uneven in width, repeating along the whole arc and on the G and T outlines.
The thin outer line of the swoosh tip ends in a ragged black wedge and sparse white stitches instead of a fine point.
The swoosh tip end has loose white stitches and a black blob that does not taper like the original.
The T fill runs in diagonal strokes unlike the G's horizontal fill, and the bevel at the T crossbar junction is broken into abrupt colour patches.
The tee top yellow band is made of crossing stitches with a ragged lower edge and hooked tip that differ from the clean flare in the art.
The G inner stem pieces are chopped into separate yellow and red blocks with a visible tuft where they meet.

L_toat_machine_hat.reason: 1: The whole interior of the badge is filled with a grey hatch fill where the original is plain white, so fabric is covered that should show and the logo reads grey-on-grey. The lettering itself is recognisable and counters stay open, but the M and the n-e join have mushed, notched stitch pile-ups, and the speed lines are heavier than the hairlines in the art. | 2: The whole interior of the badge is sewn with a light hatch fill that the white-background original does not have, which would be wasteful and visible on a hat. The black lettering and border are otherwise recognisable and clean, but the speed lines lose their taper, the M's thin inner strokes are pinched with stray bits, and a few letter joins (c, h, n) are jumbled.

faults.note: 1: Crossover stitch bars pile up where the M's diagonal stroke meets the second stem, a visible artefact not in the original. | 2: Crossed stitch bars at the top of the M's second thin diagonal form a small pile-up not in the original.
1: A short loose stitch bar sits at the junction of the M's first stem and its diagonal. | 2: A short crossing stitch bar sits where the M's thin diagonal joins the stem, an artefact not in the art.
1: Small white slits break the top of the h ascender where column stitches fail to meet. | 2: Small white slivers cut into the top of the h ascender where stitch ends do not meet.

1: The join between the n and the e is a tangle of fanning and overlapping stitches that mushes the two letters together. | 2: The i and n join at the lower left of the n is a messy overlap of fanned stitches with ragged edges and no clean stroke.

one_reader.note: The whole badge interior is sewn with a light grey diagonal hatch fill that the white-background original does not have.
The top of the M's first stem is built from stacked, misaligned column blocks with notches and small gaps, giving a lumpy, broken edge unlike the clean stem in the art.
The bottom of the n's stem fans stitches radially in a rosette instead of following the stroke.
The base of the c and the bowl of the a collapse into radial fans with a dense pile at the bottom, repeated in several lowercase letters.
The speed lines beside the To A T and above LLC are sewn as thick bars, much heavier than the tapered hairlines in the art; this repeats on every line.
The outer border satin has saw-toothed edges and a ragged apex at the top point; this repeats along the whole border.
A little nub sticks out at the left end of the upper speed line beside the C.
Many long needle-up travels cross the open field between the letters, which would need trimming.
The whole badge interior is filled with a light grey hatch fill; the original is plain white background there, so fabric should show.
Speed lines left of and right of the T are sewn as uniform 1 to 1.5 mm bars where the original has fine tapered lines, so they read heavier and blunt (repeats on all speed lines).
The top of the M's first stem is chopped into notched blocks with small gaps along its right edge compared with the clean original stem.
The slim gap between the M's first diagonal and stem is narrower and more ragged than the original.
The top of the c's terminal is a jumbled cluster of short fan stitches, blunter than the pointed original.
The n to e connection is a rough patch of overlapping stitch directions, less clean than the original stroke.
The h and i stems change stitch angle between segments with visible steps in the edge.

L_toat_beanie.reason: 1: The hexagon border, wordmark and speed lines are all present and recognisable, but the script Machine letters are lumpy and mushed where strokes join, with fan-shaped stitch pile-ups in the c, h and e. The small To A T letters have narrowed counters and a muddy A. Needs a clean-up, not a re-do. | 2: The Machine script is the weak point: the a, c, h and the joins between them are sewn with fan-shaped, shifting stitch angles that make bumpy, mushy strokes where the original has clean pen strokes. The To A T lettering and the border are sound, though the o and A counters are tight and the thin speed lines are fatter than the art.

faults.note: 1: The A of To A T is lumpy with a filled-in crossbar area, and its counter is nearly closed. | 2: The A counter is nearly closed and the crossbar fills the triangle, so the A reads as a blob compared with the open original.
1: The border corner at the top right shows a small gap and ragged join between sections. | 2: The right border corner has small bright slivers of fabric showing where the stitches turn the corner.

1: The c and h of Machine merge into a tangle of fanned stitches, and the c's inner hook is filled in. | 2: The c and h of Machine are a tangle of fanned stitch angles with a lumpy outline, so the letter forms are muddy next to the clean original strokes.

one_reader.note: The first upstroke of the M has a small pile-up of crossed stitches where its two sections meet.
The bottom of the M's inner V is notched and ragged where the stroke ends, against a clean point in the original.
The o counter is narrowed and its outline is uneven with fanning stitches.
The loop of the h at its base is a fan pile-up with a small hole, not a smooth curve.
The bowl of the final e has fan-shaped pile-ups and a stray block stitched into its counter; repeats on the n before it.
The small dash after LLC is sewn as a broken blob that does not match the thin dash in the art.
The thin speed lines under the M pulse in width and wobble along their length; the same on the lines right of LLC.
Very long needle-up jumps cross open fill across the design (for example from the right side to the LLC area); they would need trimming.
The h and i junction pile up in fan-shaped stitches and the small loop is nearly closed.
The n-e connection and the e bowl have a rough fanned bottom curve and a notch where strokes overlap, unlike the smooth original.
The a bowl bottom is built from radiating stitches with a ragged edge and a stub where the stroke ends.
The left strokes of the M have wobbly, ragged edges and a notched bottom where the original is a clean tapered stroke.
The V of the M has a small gap and ragged overlap where the two strokes meet.
A small pile of crossed stitches sits on the inner edge of the second M stroke where the original has a smooth edge.
The o in To has a tight counter and a lumpy outer outline, smaller and rounder than the squarish original.
The h ascender stroke is stepped and wavy along its length where the original is a straight tapered stroke.
The thin speed lines below the M are sewn fatter and with uneven width and blunt ends where the original tapers to a point; this repeats on the upper lines.
The period after LLC is a broken little stub instead of a clean small rectangle.

agreement_rule: two blind readers per design; a fault counts only when both place one of the same class within 3 mm; a grade counts only when both give it
